content.subject: Final patience — settlement by month-end or this gets ugly
content.body:
I'm writing this once and I want it forwarded to whichever partner actually makes decisions, because Attorney Halverson clearly does not.

I slipped on an unmarked wet floor at the Crestmoor Plaza branch of Brightline Grocers on January 4. I have the incident report with the manager's signature, I have the security footage stills your investigator already obtained, I have three witnesses, I have an orthopedist's report documenting a torn meniscus and a wrist fracture, and I have $41,300 in documented medical expenses and counting. This is not a complicated case. This is a layup.

It has been four months. Brightline's carrier opened with $22,000 in March. We countered at $185,000. Their last move was $48,000 three weeks ago. Halverson tells me we're 'building leverage.' I don't need more leverage. I need a check. I have two kids, I am behind on the second mortgage, and the bill from Pinegate Orthopedic Associates went to collections last Wednesday.

Here is what is going to happen. You are going to get me to $135,000 net to me, after fees and liens, by May 30. That is two weeks. If that number is not in writing by then, I am going to start posting. I have 14,000 followers on my page. I will post the firm name. I will post Halverson's name. I will post screenshots of every email where he told me to be patient while my credit was being destroyed. I will tag every personal injury attorney in the metro area and ask them publicly why this firm sits on cases. I have already drafted the first three posts. My sister works in PR and she has reviewed them. They are factual, they are within my rights, and they will run on the dates I have queued up unless I have a number in writing.

I am not interested in a phone call to 'manage my expectations.' I am interested in a number. Get it done.

Tatiana Pruitt
